tytul: Polish beans with sausage preserved by tyndallization: why there is no recipe here
wstep: There is no recipe here for Polish beans in tomato sauce with a lot of sausage (fasolka po bretońsku), preserved in jars by tyndallization, that is, by heating the jars several times with pauses.

ostrzezenia.tekst: Pressure canning is the only recommended method for canning meat, poultry, seafood and vegetables; using a boiling-water bath for these foods poses a real risk of botulism poisoning.
Tyndallization (repeated heating with pauses for spores to germinate) is not considered fully reliable, because some superdormant spores do not germinate between heatings.
NCHFP says not to add noodles or other pasta, rice, flour, cream, milk or other thickening agents to home-canned soups.

akapity: Botulinum spores are very hard to destroy at boiling-water temperatures.
JarAtlas has found no tested home recipe for Polish beans with sausage in jars from a checked source.
JarAtlas has a card for dried beans in tomato sauce canned in a pressure canner.
